newsitem.title: USA: Occidental Pete takes Komi Arctic charge. [CORRECTED]
newsitem.headline: Occidental Pete takes Komi Arctic charge. [CORRECTED]

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp said Thursday it took a $105 million charge in the third quarter for the write-down of its investment in a project in the Russian republic of Komi.
(Corrects project involved and drops references to British Gas, which is not in the Occidental venture).
The company offset the impact of the charge with a $100 million benefit from a reduction in federal income tax liabilities no longer required.

It reported higher than expected net income of $194 million, or $0.53 per share for the third quarter, compared with $139 million, $0.36 per share, in 1995. The First Call consensus estimate for the latest quarter was $0.43 per share.

"Our Oil and Gas division continued the excellent performance of the first six months" in the third quarter, the company said. "Chemical earnings continued to improve from the levels in the first and second quarters."
Oil and gas divisional earnings before special items were $125 million for the third quarter of 1996, compared with earnings of $46 million for the third quarter of 1995.
The increase resulted primarily from higher prices for worldwide crude oil and domestic natural gas, partially offset by higher exploration expense, Occidental said.

Natural gas transmission divisional earnings for the third quarter of 1996 were $49 million, compared with $54 million for the third quarter of 1995. The decline resulted primarily from lower transport margins, partially offset by cost savings related to the reorganization announced late in 1995.

Chemical divisional earnings before special items for the third quarter of 1996 were $190 million, compared with earnings of $252 million for the third quarter of 1995. The decline resulted primarily from decreased profit margins in petrochemicals, PVC resins and caustic soda, partially offset by improvements in profits from specialty chemicals.

Interest expense in the third quarter of 1996 was $107 million, compared with $133 million for the third quarter of 1995. The decline is primarily attributable to lower average interest rates and lower average debt levels resulting primarily from redemptions of high-coupon debt.
